summary: A spec-only split commit whose entire deliverable is the three successor rows' criteria, so the criteria ARE the code under review. F1-F5 are all discharged as described: the union clause exists as M5.45c criterion 5 and cites ADR-0043's assignment; d(1) says 'K = 64 RUNS ON ONE CONSUMER' and explains why 64 consumers is non-falsifiable; d(1b) assigns the startup half; d's State cell says c and d are independent; and zero M5.45b references remain outside review/ (which is an archive). All eleven repointed Java citations name the right successor row. Two majors remain, both in the newly written union criterion and both invisible to every gate. (1) The span `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` is not openable by the only reader in the tree: SegmentReader.open refuses a prefix twice over, on the footer magic and on the per-entry bounds check. (2) The union has no home in `client`: production builds one ConsumerClient per RunKey, so 'K runs on ONE consumer' is not constructible there, and a counting-fetcher case against a single fetcher instance passes while production still issues one ranged GET per run per node -- the shards-per-node rate the clause exists to forbid. Two minors on d(1b)'s justification and on two clauses of SPEC criterion 7 that the split drops.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:64 -- M5.45c criterion 5, final clause: 'AND THE REQUEST SPANS `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))`, header included, because `codecFlags` is per run in the DIRECTORY and a slice-only read cannot decompress what it fetched (ADR-0043)'
findings.claim: The span reasons correctly about codecFlags -- the directory IS at the front (SegmentFormat.java:12-18: PREAMBLE 32 B, then DIRECTORY, then DATA, then FOOTER 24 B) and byteStart IS absolute from byte 0 (SegmentWriter.java:98 sets byteStart = PREAMBLE_BYTES + headerLen and advances by block length), so [0, max(byteStart+byteLen)) does contain the preamble, every directory entry and every run this node wants. But it is NOT a decodable object for the only reader in the tree. SegmentReader.open refuses such a prefix for two independent reasons: (a) SegmentReader.java:68-71 computes f = segment.length - FOOTER_BYTES and throws 'segment is truncated: no footer magic' unless FOOTER_MAGIC sits in the last 24 bytes -- a prefix ending at max(byteStart+byteLen) has no footer at all; (b) SegmentReader.java:89 validates EVERY directory entry with `byteStart + byteLen > f` and throws 'run i points outside the segment' -- and a prefix by construction truncates the runs this node did not want. ConsumerClient.decodeInto (ConsumerClient.java:78) calls SegmentReader.open(delivery.segment()) on the whole array with no partial-read path, so the criterion as written cannot be satisfied end to end.
findings.failure_scenario: The taker of M5.45c implements the fetcher exactly as criterion 5 specifies: one ranged GET for [0, max(byteStart+byteLen)), handed to ConsumerClient as delivery.segment(). Every `direct` delivery then throws UncheckedIOException('segment is truncated: no footer magic') at ConsumerClient.java:78 before a single record is decoded -- for a node holding one run as much as for one holding 64. The counting-fetcher case in criterion 5 still passes (it counts requests, not decodes), so the row can close green while `direct` delivers nothing; M5.45e is where it surfaces, one row later, as 'all three modes deliver byte-identical records' failing for the third mode.
findings.suggested_fix: State the span that is actually decodable and keep the cost claim, which survives either way: one contiguous request covering the preamble, the directory, the wanted runs AND the 24-byte footer is the whole object when the last wanted run is not the last run -- i.e. `[0, objectLen)`, still ONE request per (node, segment), still flat in segments. If a true prefix is wanted, say that SegmentReader needs a prefix mode (footer check skipped, entry bounds checked only for the runs present) and give that change a row, because it is a reader change in `format` that no row owns today.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:64 -- M5.45c criterion 5: 'ASSERT IT WITH A COUNTING FETCHER: K runs of one segment on one consumer cost ONE fetch, at K = 64 RUNS rather than 64 consumers', read against criterion 1 ('an interface in `client` taking a `Grant` plus a byte range and yielding bytes')
findings.claim: The clause fixes F2's K-overloading but leaves the sharing unit unnamed, and in `client` there is no object that holds K runs. ConsumerClient's constructor takes exactly ONE RunKey (ConsumerClient.java:44-57) and subscribes it; decodeInto handles one Delivery at a time off a per-client ArrayBlockingQueue. Production creates one ConsumerClient PER RunKey -- NodeSubscriptions.java:78, `e = new Entry(new ConsumerClient(transport, k, queueCapacity))`, keyed by RunKey -- and NodeSubscriptions lives in `plugin`, which criteria 1-3 put outside this row's scope. So 'one consumer' holding 64 runs does not exist on the client side, and a fetcher whose seam is (grant, range) can only union by holding state ACROSS calls, i.e. per fetcher INSTANCE. The criterion never says the instance is shared per node/process rather than per ConsumerClient, and it never prices the memory of the coalesced bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: The taker writes CoalescingFetcher, feeds one instance 64 (grant, range) pairs for one segmentKey in a unit case, counts ONE underlying fetch, and marks criterion 5 green. They then wire it the natural way -- constructed inside ConsumerClient, where the fetcher is needed -- and production, which has one ConsumerClient per RunKey, gets one fetcher per run: a catch-up node holding ~400 runs of an 8 MiB segment issues ~400 consumer-side ranged GETs against one object. That is the shards-per-node rate non-negotiable 6 forbids by name and the exact defect this criterion was added to prevent, and GrantIssuer's own javadoc records that consumer-side GETs are invisible to CountingBinStore, so no meter, no gate and no other criterion sees it. The second half is memory: unioning across K deliveries that arrive on K independent queues and are decoded at K independent readNext calls requires either a per-node cache holding the whole 8 MiB segment or a barrier waiting for all K -- neither is named, and the cache is per-node client memory nobody has budgeted.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the unit in the criterion: ONE fetcher instance per node (or per process), shared by every ConsumerClient on it, and say that the counting case must drive the 64 runs through whatever production shares -- which means either M5.45c widens to the ConsumerClient/NodeSubscriptions wiring and says so, or the criterion states that it asserts the coalescer in isolation and hands the 'one fetcher per node, not per ConsumerClient' wiring to a named row (M5.45e or a new one). Add the memory consequence of holding a coalesced segment, or say explicitly that it is deferred and to where.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:65 -- M5.45d criterion 1b: 'per-publish construction would satisfy every other criterion here while moving the refusal back to first use, which is what it exists to prevent'
findings.claim: The criterion (construct the issuer once per pod) is right and checkable, but its stated consequence is false in the tree as of M5.43. DefaultIngest.java:224 already calls storeCapabilities.requirePresignedUrls() inside the constructor under `if (config.directEnabled())`, and GrantIssuer's constructor makes the identical call (GrantIssuer.java:117). A pod with directEnabled on a backend that cannot sign therefore fails to CONSTRUCT DefaultIngest, before any publish and regardless of where the issuer is built -- so a per-publish GrantIssuer can never be the first place the refusal fires.
findings.failure_scenario: The taker of M5.45d writes the case the clause implies -- make the issuer per-publish and assert the refusal arrives late -- and finds it unwritable, because the pod cannot start at all on a non-signing backend with `direct` enabled. They then either weaken the criterion to something tautological or spend a round rediscovering M5.43's call site. The real reasons to hoist the construction (one capability check per pod rather than per publish, and one place for the ceiling) go unstated.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep 1b and restate the why: the startup refusal is already made at DefaultIngest.java:224, so what 1b buys is that the ISSUER is a pod-lifetime collaborator rather than a per-publish allocation with a per-publish capability check -- and say how it is pinned (e.g. the hub takes a GrantIssuer, or a counting construction fake asserts exactly one construction across N publishes).

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:65 -- M5.45d criteria (2) and (3), against the original M5.45b criterion 2 at line 63: 'SPEC criterion 7 in full on the assembled path: TTL <= 60s (ADR-0010), read-only, one key, a backend without `presign` refused AT STARTUP and not at first fetch, and the grant in NO log, trace or error message'
findings.claim: Re-deriving the union of c/d/e against the original row one more time: the five clauses of 'criterion 7 in full' land as TTL -> d(2), startup refusal -> d(1b), no-log -> d(3) -- and READ-ONLY and ONE KEY land nowhere in c, d or e. One key is pinned at unit level (GrantIssuerTest.java:277, 'criterion 3: one key, and it is the key asked for') and read-only is a real-backend property that M5.37/M5.42 already reassigned to M9, so the loss is the ASSEMBLED-PATH half of two clauses rather than the property itself. But the original row said 'in full on the assembled path', and nothing now says those two are carried elsewhere.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45d closes with its four criteria green, and a reader of the milestone concludes SPEC criterion 7 is satisfied on the assembled path. The grant the hub actually mints is never asserted to be scoped to the one segment key on that path -- a minting site that passed, say, the delta's first segment key (the ADR-0032 silent data error AssembledServingPathTest:339 records for the push label) would satisfy d(1), d(2), d(3) and d(4) and hand a consumer a grant for another pod's object. The unit case at GrantIssuerTest:277 does not see the hub's call site.
findings.suggested_fix: One clause in d: the grant is scoped to the segment key the push names, asserted on the assembled path; and one sentence saying read-only rests on M9's first capable backend, which is where M5.37 and M5.42 already put it.

verified: F1 discharged: M5.45c criterion 5 exists (backlog.md:64), cites ADR-0043's assignment of security.md rule 3's range half, and says explicitly that the split would otherwise have left the obligation with no owner. Its two defects are the two majors above, not its absence.

F2 discharged: M5.45d criterion 1 reads 'K = 64 RUNS ON ONE CONSUMER', states that 64 consumers holding one run each yields 64 grants under BOTH implementations, and quotes M5.40a's measured survivor accurately -- M5.40a's cell does say 'every caller in the tree subscribes one RunKey per Subscriber so K is always 1'.
F3 discharged: M5.45d criterion 1b assigns the issuer's construction site. Its justification is minor finding 3.

F4 discharged: M5.45d's State cell now reads 'M5.45c and M5.45d are INDEPENDENT ... Only M5.45e needs both', and M5.45e's State cell says it depends on both. The dependency graph is consistent with the module split (d touches ingest, c touches client).

F5 discharged: `grep -rn 'M5\.45b'` over the tree, excluding build/ and .git, returns hits only in review/verdicts/ and review/overrides.md -- archives of past rounds, correctly historical. Zero in src/main, src/test or clusterTest.

All eleven repointed Java citations name the row that owns what the sentence describes: Delivery.java:17 -> c (the client type that gains the grant, criterion c(2)); Grant.java:35 -> d (the SignedUrl->Grant adapter is ingest-side minting); DefaultIngest.java:69 -> d (the serving path); SubscriptionHub.java:67, :296, :413 and the DIRECT arm's message at :434 -> d (all hub-side); SubscriptionHub.java:430 correctly splits 'a grant (M5.45d) and a client-side byte source (M5.45c)'; AssembledServingPathTest.java:339 -> d (the key the minted grant is scoped to); DirectEnablementTest.java:128 -> d (builds GrantIssuer under directEnabled); StoreFakes.java:259 and :276 -> d (the clamp assertion and the fake's first caller).

ADR-0043's Status note is accurate against the backlog rows it names: c owns the seam and the union, d owns minting/coalescing/clamp, e owns the end-to-end byte-identity claim, and the three sentences the note replaces ('mint a grant, wire GrantIssuer, or give the consumer a way to fetch with one') are each reassigned. The date matches today.

Request rate: this diff creates, moves and removes no object-store request -- it is prose only. The rate it SPECIFIES for the future is the subject of the two majors: as written, M5.45c criterion 5 is satisfiable with one consumer-side ranged GET per run per node still in place.

SegmentFormat/SegmentWriter/SegmentReader read directly to check the span claim rather than taken from the ADR: directory at the front, byteStart absolute, footer mandatory in open(), per-entry bounds checked against length-minus-footer.
honesty_judgement: The split itself is honest and the rows are well shaped: three rows, each with a criterion that can fail, and the State cells say what depends on what. The round-1 findings were answered in substance rather than by deleting the clause that provoked them, which is the failure mode this repo has recorded before. What the fixes did NOT do is check the new criteria against the tree: criterion 5's span is repeated from M5.44's cell and ADR-0043 without anyone opening SegmentReader, and 1b's justification is repeated from criterion 7's wording without anyone opening DefaultIngest's constructor, which M5.43 changed. Both are the restated-prose pattern one layer up -- a claim inherited from a document rather than measured -- and both land in a commit whose only deliverable is the claims.
